basis: Written before any E1b run, from the lambda sweep (outputs/lambda_sweep: answers world, training annotators, seeds 100-109) and the seconds-onset check at lambda = 1 (outputs/lapse_seconds_check, final test).
decision: Lambda stays 1.0 whatever the outcome; this is a sensitivity check only.
P1: Reproduction, answers world: QMDP average accuracy is higher at lambda 0.25 than at 1.25 (sweep: 74.9 vs 69.3), and QMDP minus always-2-choice is not clearly negative at 0.25 (sweep: about +1.0) but clearly negative at 1.0 (sweep: -3.9).
P2: Mechanism, both worlds: QMDP collects more answers, and more answers after the lapse, at lambda 1.25 than at 0.25.
P3: Main: QMDP average accuracy falls less from lambda 0.25 to 1.25 in the seconds world than in the answers world (timing the lapse in seconds removes part of the throughput penalty).
P4: Main: in the seconds world, QMDP minus its strongest rival (the best of greedy, greedy-plus-rest and fatigue-blind at the same lambda, always-verify and always-2-choice) is higher at lambda 0.25 than at lambda 1.0, i.e. the remaining Lapse loss is partly driven by lambda.
P5: Reproduction on other people: at lambda 1.0 in the seconds world, QMDP is behind its strongest rival (development check -1.70, final test -1.84 at 200 labels).
